title: How a P-Trap Works: The Defensive Water Seal
description: The P-trap located beneath a sink is a simple yet critical component of every sanitary drainage system. Its primary function is to hold a standing pocket of water, known as the trap seal, between the fixture and the main waste line. This standing water creates a physical barrier that stops sewer gases, foul odors, and pests from entering the room through the drain basin. Every time the sink is used, incoming water displaces the old water, continuously refreshing the seal. Plumbers must ensure correct trap depth and proper installation slope to prevent self-siphoning or dry traps.

How a P-Trap Works: The Defensive Water Seal

The P-trap located beneath a sink is a simple yet critical component of every sanitary drainage system. Its primary function is to hold a standing pocket of water, known as the trap seal, between the fixture and the main waste line. This standing water creates a physical barrier that stops sewer gases, foul odors, and pests from entering the room through the drain basin. Every time the sink is used, incoming water displaces the old water, continuously refreshing the seal. Plumbers must ensure correct trap depth and proper installation slope to prevent self-siphoning or dry traps.
